items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the real property actions and proceedings law, in relation to designating a party to accept service in the event a property becomes vacant during the foreclosure process
items.lawSection: Real Property Actions and Proceedings Law
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S1944

 TITLE OF BILL :

An act to amend the real property actions and proceedings law, in
relation to designating a party to accept service in the event a
property becomes vacant during the foreclosure process


 PURPOSE :

Enactment of this legislation would require a lender who starts a
foreclosure proceeding to designate a party that will be responsible
for accepting service of any court actions if the property becomes
vacant during the foreclosure process.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

Section 1 amends the real property and proceedings law by adding a new
section 1305 requiring that an agent be designated prior to the
initiation of a foreclosure. Further states that such designation
shall be filed in the county clerk's office and shall include the
address at which such designated agent will accept service, which must
be located within the county where such filing takes place. This
filing shall remain in effect for a period of three years.

 EXISTING LAW :

Under current law there are no designations for service, and service
is generally assumed to be accepted by the legal representative of the
foreclosing entity.

 JUSTIFICATION :

This would provide a municipal agency or other entity with an avenue
to serve a lender who intends to foreclose on a property. There is
presently no statute written designating an agent to be served, and
therefore once the subject property becomes vacant during the
foreclosure process, an agent will have been designated by the lending
authority to be served during this process.

In the past, it was assumed that the legal representative of the
lending entity would be the agent for service. This would provide a
clear, concise way to serve process on the foreclosing authority.
This legislation was recommended by the Mayor's Anti-Flipping Task
Force in Buffalo, New York in an effort to reduce the number of vacant
properties in the city and to establish responsibility for repairs and
maintenance.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

New bill - 2008 - Referred to Judiciary.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

None to New York State.

 LOCAL FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

None.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect immediately.
